intro: PDF to JPG turns each page of a PDF into an image, ready to post on a website or social network, drop into a presentation or send through a messaging app. The conversion runs in your browser with PDFium, the same rendering engine used by Chromium browsers, so the document never leaves your device.

Set the resolution between 72 and 600 dots per inch; the default of 144 suits screens, while higher values give sharp images for printing. JPEG quality goes from 1 to 100%, and you can get the images in colour or greyscale.

Pick the pages you want with ranges such as “1-3, 5” or the odd and even shortcuts. Each image is named after the PDF followed by the page number, and when there is more than one they download together in a ZIP. You can also ask for a single tall image with every page stacked.
To protect your device, each page has a pixel limit: if the requested resolution exceeds it, the image is scaled down just enough to avoid running out of memory.

faq.a: 144 dpi for viewing on screen; 300 dpi or more if you are going to print the image.

faq.q: Can I export only some pages?
faq.a: Yes, type the range under “Pages”, for example 2-4 or 1, 3.
Use PDF to PNG, which saves pages losslessly and supports black and white.

faq.q: Can I convert several PDFs at once?
faq.a: Yes. Add as many files as you need: inside the ZIP there will be one folder per document with its numbered pages.
